subject: Post-demo discovery: performance gates, streaming needs & regional residency checklist
messages:
From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@quantify.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Alec Moreno <alec.moreno@quantify.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: demo + a few performance/residency questions

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful walkthrough. A couple of items we need answers on before we can take this to procurement and security: 

1) Latency targets: our product needs p95 generation latency under 250ms for short responses (~<200 tokens) in the US region and p95 <300ms in EU. Can Redwood hit these with the hosted API, or would we need Dedicated?

2) Streaming: we stream token-by-token to our web clients. We need confirmation that the API will forward partial tokens with max 100ms chunking and not buffer until response completion. Any limitations on streaming with batching or quantized models?

3) Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency of 120 simultaneous users during peak (each making ~1 req/min, average response 120 tokens). Burst QPS could be up to 400 req/min for short windows. We want a sense of recommended config and autoscaling behavior.

4) Regional routing & data residency: we want EU-customer traffic and logs to remain in EU (for GDPR). For APAC we prefer Singapore region for lower latency. Can you outline how routing + residency works for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments?

5) Contract/controls: we’ll need explicit contract language on data residency and a runbook for SOC2 artifacts and log retention.

Next step: can you share a short mutual action plan and a perf checklist we can use to validate? We’ll also share a small sample workload (prompts + expected token lengths) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Linh
Product Ops | QuantifyAI

--
QuantifyAI, Inc.
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@quantify.ai>
Cc: Alec Moreno <alec.moreno@quantify.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + a few performance/residency questions

Linh — great questions, and thanks for the clear ask list. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a short perf checklist and a mutual action plan draft.

Recap on capabilities (short answers):
- Latency (p95): Hosted API can meet p95 ~150–220ms for short responses in US depending on prompt size and concurrency. EU numbers typically add 20–80ms depending on region and instance placement. For guaranteed 300ms p95 under load we often recommend Redwood Dedicated or a pinned Dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
- Streaming: Full token-level streaming supported. Streaming works with batching; Redwood streams whenever first token is available and emits intermediate chunks. Max chunking latency is configurable (we can target ~100ms chunks). Note: some extreme batching/quantization profiles can add micro-batching delay — we’ll capture this in the perf run.
- Throughput & concurrency: For 120 concurrent users (mean response ~120 tokens) the hosted autoscaler should handle bursts to ~400 rps-equivalent short-term, but sustained throughput with strict SLOs is best on Dedicated. Our quick heuristic: 1 x medium Dedicated pool ~= 250 concurrent short-generation sessions with p95 headroom; we’ll validate with your exact prompts.
- Regional routing & residency: Hosted routing is region-aware and we can route by client IP/region. However, hosted logs/metrics may traverse central control plane; if you require EU-only data storage and logs, the Private (VPC) or Dedicated with EU-only tenancy is the recommended path.
- Contract items: we can provide region-scoped data residence clauses and SOC2 artifacts. Priya (cc’d) will cover security evidence and contract language.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- You: Share sample prompt set, token distribution, and an expected QPS profile (by EOD tomorrow).
- Us: Run a 48-hour perf validation in US and EU regions (we’ll simulate concurrency and bursts you provide). Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latency matrix, token cost estimation, streaming chunk timings, and a short list of tuning recommendations (batch size, quantization profile).
- Legal/Security: Priya to follow up on residency wording and SOC2 artifacts.
- Timing: Could we run the perf validation starting Tue 3/3? If earlier is needed we can try to start 3/1.

Attachments: redwood-perf-checklist.csv, mutual-action-plan-QuantifyAI.docx

Would love to confirm start date and the data package. I’ll loop in Priya on residency specifics and Marissa on commercial next steps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0212

Redwood Inference

Thanks — that recap helps. We’ll package the sample prompts and a short QPS timeline by EOD today. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For EU residency — does Dedicated with EU-only tenancy guarantee that request/response bodies and logs never leave EU? We need that spelled out for procurement.
2) Streaming chunking: if micro-batching is enabled to improve cost, will that ever prevent per-token streaming semantics (i.e., will the client see partial tokens delayed)?

If you can give short clear answers to those two items we’ll lock in a 3/3 start.

—Alec
Head of Platform Eng | QuantifyAI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alec Moreno <alec.moreno@quantify.ai>, Linh Tran <linh.tran@quantify.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + a few performance/residency questions

Alec — quick answers to your two bullet items + implementation options we recommend: 

1) EU residency guarantee: Dedicated with EU-only tenancy and Private (VPC) deployments both support an explicit data residency configuration. For Dedicated EU tenancy we guarantee customer data (request bodies, generated outputs, telemetry, and logs) are stored only in EU regions and processed on EU-hosted instances. The control plane may surface metadata but we can contractually bind processing and storage to EU zones; Priya will provide the exact contract language and a short SOC2+residency addendum.

2) Streaming + micro-batching: Redwood streams tokens as soon as the first token is available. Micro-batching optimizes GPU utilization by grouping concurrent requests but does not change token ordering or token-level delivery semantics; worst-case impact is a ~20–80ms batching window depending on load and batch config. In short: clients will still receive incremental tokens (we can target <100ms chunk latency in tuning).

Implementation recommendation:
- PoC (fastest): Hosted API perf validation in US + EU to reproduce latency characteristics quickly (no residency guarantee required for evaluation).
- PoC (compliant): Spin up a short-term Dedicated EU pool (pin tenancy) for the EU perf run so the team can validate both latency and residency constraints under realistic conditions. This also makes commercial uplift visible before a Private deployment.

I’m proposing we start the Hosted PoC on Tue 3/3 and run an EU Dedicated run the week after (3/10–3/12) if that works for you. Priya will reach out with contractual language and the SOC2 artifact list by Monday. Marissa will coordinate commercial terms once the perf runs validate the SLO targets.

If that schedule works I’ll put the PoC kickoff on the calendar and mark the expected deliverables.

Thanks,
Aditya
